_meta.indication: ZEMDRI is an aminoglycoside antibacterial indicated in patients 18 years of age or older for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis, and Enterobacter cloacae.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study ACHN-490-009 (Study 009), also referred to as Trial 1
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, noninferiority trial comparing IV plazomicin to IV meropenem, with an option to switch to oral therapy after at least 4-5 days of IV treatment.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults >=18 years with complicated urinary tract infection, including acute pyelonephritis; mMITT median age 64 years, 52.8% female, 99.5% White, with about 41.8% having pyelonephritis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoint of composite cure (clinical success and microbiologic eradication) in the mMITT population at the Day 5 and Test-of-Cure (TOC) visits.
pivotal_trials.n: 609 patients randomized; mMITT population 388 (191 plazomicin, 197 meropenem)
pivotal_trials.result: At Day 5, composite cure 88% (168/191) plazomicin vs 91.4% (180/197) meropenem, difference -3.4 (95% CI -10.0, 3.1); at TOC, 81.7% (156/191) plazomicin vs 70.1% (138/197) meropenem, difference 11.6 (95% CI 2.7, 20.3); plazomicin was noninferior within the prespecified -15% margin.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=1%) are decreased renal function, diarrhea, hypertension, headache, nausea, vomiting and hypotension. In Trial 1, adverse reactions associated with renal function occurred in 3.6% (11/303) of ZEMDRI patients vs 1.3% (4/301) meropenem, and serum creatinine increases >=0.5 mg/dL occurred in 7% (21/300) vs 4% (12/297).
target_moa: Plazomicin is an aminoglycoside (derived from sisomicin) that binds to the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, thereby inhibiting protein synthesis and exerting concentration-dependent bactericidal activity; it retains activity in the presence of many aminoglycoside modifying enzymes.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for NEPHROTOXICITY, OTOTOXICITY, NEUROMUSCULAR BLOCKADE and FETAL HARM: nephrotoxicity (greater risk in renal impairment, elderly, concomitant nephrotoxic drugs); ototoxicity (hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo, possibly irreversible); neuromuscular blockade; and fetal harm in pregnant women.

advisory_committee.vote: Antimicrobials Drug Advisory Committee met May 03, 2018; voted 15 Yes, 0 No, 0 Abstain that substantial evidence of safety and effectiveness was provided for the cUTI indication (for BSI: 4 Yes, 11 No).

citations.quote: December 12, 2014: Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation was granted for the indications of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP), ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP), complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAIs), cUTI, and catheter-related BSI.

summary.text: Plazomicin received QIDP designation (December 12, 2014), Fast Track designation for serious/life-threatening CRE infections, and Breakthrough Therapy designation for bloodstream infections due to certain Enterobacteriaceae; the NDA was reviewed under Priority review and approved first cycle on June 25, 2018 for the cUTI indication, following a 15-0 Advisory Committee vote supporting the cUTI indication.

citations.quote: December 12, 2014: Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation was granted for the indications of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP), ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP), complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAIs), cUTI, and catheter-related BSI.

Plazomicin was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation for the following indications: hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP), ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP), complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAIs), cUTI, and catheter-related BSI, Fast Track designation for the treatment of serious and life-threatening infections due to carbapenem resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) and Breakthrough Therapy designation for the treatment of BSIs caused by certain Enterobacteriaceae in patients who have limited or no alternative treatment options.
This NDA was discussed at the Antimicrobials Drug Advisory Committee meeting on May 03, 2018. The committee was asked to vote on two questions.
